channel.title: Pier & Point · on the ground

item.title: Added · Mission Bay South Block 12 West: On October 6, 2026, OCII's Commission voted to adopt the…
item.description: On October 6, 2026, OCII's Commission voted to adopt the resolution authorizing a memorandum of understanding with FOCIL-MB for Block 12 West. Source: OCII Commission minutes, regular meeting of Oct 6, 2026, p. 5 (https://sfocii.org/files/minutes/2026-10/20261006_OCII%20Minutes.pdf); OCII Resolution No. 23-2026, headed Adopted October 6, 2026 (https://sfocii.org/files/inline-files/2026023.pdf).

item.title: Milestone · Potrero Power Station Block 11: Mayor approves the Amended and Restated… (Oct 13, 2026)
item.description: Mayor approves the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): Legistar lists both as 'Status: Passed' with 'Final action: 10/13/2026', 'Enactment date: 10/13/2026' and enactment numbers 208-26 (File 260724) and 209-26 (File 260770), and a history row '10/13/2026 ... Mayor ... APPROVED' for each. The Board's final passage on October 6, 2026 (11 ayes) is the previous entry on this timeline. October 13, 2026 is the enactment date, from the Clerk of the Board's listing (page read October 14 and again October 17, 2026); it is an event date. Both ordinances provide 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment' (File 260770 §5(a), p. 56 of its 'Leg Final' attachment; File 260724, p. 10 of its attachment); counted from October 13, 2026 that is November 13, 2026, a legal date computed by Pier & Point and not printed in the text. (Oct 13, 2026). item.title: Expected · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: Expected, not scheduled: the… (~2029)
item.description: Expected, not scheduled: the project is expected to open for use in 2029, subject to funding. The month differs by source: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post, "seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029", and the April 14 presentation, "Open for use expected June 2029"), December 2029 (SFCTA's April 14 packet, project description: "have the project open for use by December 2029, subject to funding availability"; its allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029) and "project completion by the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). Construction was not yet funded in April 2026; the FTA announced a $14.1 million award in September 2026, but no source gives a construction schedule. (~2029). Source: San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-28; San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-14; The Voice of San Francisco, 2026-10-06.
item.source: San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-28; San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-14; The Voice of San Francisco, 2026-10-06

item.title: Added · A second set of research claims about the 16 records that had deliberately been left…
item.description: A second set of research claims about the 16 records that had deliberately been left undated was verified. Confirmed and added: Mission Bay Block 34 gained a May 2020 UC Regents preliminary-plans item and its August 2024 completion date firmed to the exact day (Aug 27), while a claimed April 2021 garage-construction-start date was checked and rejected, because a Commercial Property Executive article directly contradicts it, showing the garage broke ground after, not before, the clinical building. Park P10 gained two real earlier-stage milestones from a directly read EPA/DTSC brownfields fact sheet that names "Mission Bay Park P10" specifically, and a 2011 press-tour article; a companion Board of Supervisors citation given for a different record (P11/P11A) turned out, on direct Legistar lookup, to refer to an unrelated Graffiti Advisory Board appointment and was rejected outright. Avalon at Mission Bay II gained a real Q1 2005 construction-start date from the developer's own SEC-filed earnings release. 255 Berry's existing 2004 completion milestone had its source upgraded from a generic listing search to the developer's own project page. Mission Creek Park (the P3 extension) gained an October 2022 completion date from a Landscape Performance Series case study, answering an open question already noted on the record (whether a fall-2021 target opening actually happened; it slipped a year further). For two records (the P26 interchange wedge and Block 22) the claimed dates were confirmed as flat misattributions: the cited Port Commission/Lotus Water material is entirely about the already-tracked Bayfront Park (P22), not either record, so nothing was added to either. Five more records (The Beacon, Mission Bay Commons, the Creek Park's own P1-P3 segment as distinct from P3, and the three UCSF garage/utility-plant records) returned no independently confirmable date and were left as they were, several because realestate.ucsf.edu persistently blocks automated access. Superseded the same day: Clark Construction's own press release states the garage portion started in April 2021, so the April 2021 date rejected above was restored by the next set of research checks. A September 2026 accuracy check noted that the outcomes listed here for P11/P11A, Avalon II, 255 Berry, Mission Creek Park P3 and P26/Block 22 come from Legistar, SEC and Landscape Performance Series pages that were not re-read in that check, and that the May 2020 Regents item and Aug 27, 2024 completion for Block 34 could not be read (realestate.ucsf.edu, stantec.com and commercialsearch.com return 403). Source: UC Regents, Finance and Capital Strategies Committee meeting notice, 2020-05-19 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/may20/fin-5.19.pdf); Commercial Property Executive, 2024 (https://www.commercialsearch.com/news/ucsf-opens-228m-health-care-facility/); US EPA Region 9, Brownfields RLF Success Stories, California DTSC Subgrants, 2012-07 (https://archive.epa.gov/region9/brownfields/archive/web/pdf/r9-rlf-fs-subgrants.pdf); AvalonBay Communities Q1 2005 earnings release, Attachment 7 (investors.avalonbay.com); Landscape Architecture Foundation, Mission Creek Stormwater Park case study (https://www.landscapeperformance.org/case-study-briefs/mission-creek); Clark Construction, 2021-09-23 (https://www.clarkconstruction.com/news/clark-breaks-ground-ucsfs-new-clinical-building-mission-bay).

item.title: Added · A third set of research claims was verified, under ground rules set after the two earlier…
item.description: A third set of research claims was verified, under ground rules set after the two earlier sets. Citations were real and quotable far more often this time, but two of the 13 claims were still rejected before verification began, because both cited real documents describing a different physical parcel from the one tracked here (Block 22 vs. Bayfront Park/P22, confirmed about 500m apart and matching UCSF's own "Koret Quad" label; the P26 interchange wedge vs. the real, separately named Mariposa Park, confirmed through San Francisco's Legistar API, where the cited ordinance's own title places it on a different street). Of the remaining 11, confirmed and added: Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 gained two 2018 structural-steel milestones (Mortenson's own steel-fabrication page, distinct from the arena's steel package) and a joint-venture formation note (Alexandria Real Estate's own SEC filing); Mission Bay Commons gained a narrower, accurately worded Nov 2011 completion milestone for Park P16 specifically (the source names only P16, not P17, and says "recently completed," not "dedicated," as the fuller claim implied); Mission Bay Block 34 gained a real April 2021 garage-construction-start date from Clark Construction's own press release, reversing the earlier rejection of the same date (which had relied on a vaguer secondary paraphrase). Caught and rejected: P11/P11A's claimed Board of Supervisors File #190755 was re-checked against Legistar's API and confirmed, again, not to exist; UCSF's 1670 Owens Garage citation turned out to be about a different, separately addressed UCSF garage (1625 Owens St, serving the Rutter Center) three streets away. Flagged, not resolved: whether the Mission Creek Park P1-P3 record actually belongs to Mission Bay North's own NP1/NP2 open-space system rather than the Mission Bay South labels it currently carries. Left as they were: the UCSF Preliminary Utilities Plant and part of the Third Street Garage's completion date, both blocked because realestate.ucsf.edu refused every access attempt, including through the Wayback Machine, which was itself unreachable. The Third Street Garage did gain a general-contractor fact (Overaa Construction) confirming its identity and giving 882 parking stalls (the contractor's own project page); an 822-space figure from a 2003 pre-construction budget item was cited but could not be found in the September 2026 accuracy check, so the discrepancy is unconfirmed. That check also found that, of the Block 22 / Mariposa Park, File #190755, 1670 Owens / 1625 Owens, Mortenson and Alexandria SEC findings above, only 'Koret Quad' as a real UCSF name was confirmed (Architectural Record, UC Regents Mar 2016); the rest were not re-read. Source: Mortenson (https://mortenson.com/news-insights/chase-center-structural-steel); Alexandria Real Estate Equities Q4 2017 supplemental (SEC filing, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001035443/000103544318000022/a4q17ex991supp.htm); US EPA, 2011-11-04 (https://www.epa.gov/archive/epapages/newsroom_archive/newsreleases/f331b33bcc8cb8cf8525793e00531a9a.html); Clark Construction, 2021-09-23 (https://www.clarkconstruction.com/news/clark-breaks-ground-ucsfs-new-clinical-building-mission-bay); Overaa Construction, UCSF Mission Bay Building 23B Parking Structure (https://www.overaa.com/projects/ucsf-mission-bay-building-23b-parking-structure/).

item.title: Added · Four schedule updates checked against official records (Port Commission, UC Regents, SF…
item.description: Four schedule updates checked against official records (Port Commission, UC Regents, SF Rec & Park), prompted by a third-party research summary that needed independent checking: (1) Mission Bay Block 16A: the UC Regents approved the UCSF Bakar Ear & Hearing Institute in May 2026 (a 5-story, 150,000 sq ft building), with completion targeted 2029 and occupancy 2030, added as this block's first named project and first expected-completion milestone. (2) Mission Rock Phase 2: the Port Commission approved a $10M pre-development investment (Resolution 26-34, June 9 2026) to accelerate Phase 2; the memo's own schedule frames 2027-2029 as alternative construction-start scenarios contingent on securing anchor tenants, so no single expected-completion date was added, only the June 9 event. (3) Mission Bay Parks P7 and P9 gained the same Future Parks Project schedule (construction targeted late 2028, opening targeted early 2030) already shown for the interim west Commons parcels, closing a gap where two parcels in the same bundled project were missing it. (4) Mission Bay Parks P2 and P8 gained a Dec 2015 LRPMP plan-origin date (matching P7/P9) plus the Mission Creek Park South Extension project's construction-start target (late 2026/early 2027 per sfrecpark.org); no completion date was added since the project's own page lists it as TBD. A September 2026 accuracy check found that the Bakar Ear & Hearing Institute details in (1) (5 stories, 150,000 sq ft, completion 2029, occupancy 2030) rest on a UCSF News item that could not be read and are unconfirmed; the Port memo confirms (2), and the SF Rec & Park project pages confirm (3) and (4). The same check found the June 2026 Port memo names no Phase 2 parcels, so an earlier parenthetical listing Blocks C, D1, D2 and the Channel Street open space in Phase 2 was removed as unsupported by it. Source: Port of San Francisco, Item 11A memo, June 2026 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/item_11a_mission_rock_phase_2_update_and_port_capital.pdf); SF Rec & Park, Mission Bay Future Parks Project (https://sfrecpark.org/1832/Mission-Bay-Future-Parks-Project); SF Rec & Park, Mission Creek Park South Extension Project (https://sfrecpark.org/1833/Mission-Creek-Park-South-Extension-Proje); UCSF News, May 2026 (ucsf.edu/news/2026/05/431886; not read, details unconfirmed).

item.description: Mission Rock construction schedules: none of the 13 unfinished records gained an expected completion. The 2018 Disposition and Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance (Exhibit B2) places Blocks C, D1 and D2 in Phase 2, E in Phase 3, and H, I and J in Phase 4, with horizontal-infrastructure target dates of May 2023 (Phase 2), August 2024 (Phase 3) and February 2025 (Phase 4), all already passed with none of those phases begun (the Port's October 2023 finding that Phase 2 is 'not currently financially feasible' has had no revised schedule since, per every Port Commission memo checked through February 2026). A target date that has already passed can't be shown as expected, and no revised phase date or whole-project buildout year is stated anywhere. Block K's phase after a 2019 parcel swap, and phases for Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane, Channel Wharf and TAFB Paseo, are not stated in any document found either. All 13 records stay on the 2038+ cap, and each record notes what was checked. A September 2026 accuracy check found that the DDA's Exhibit B2 itself was not read, so the phase assignments and the May 2023, Aug 2024 and Feb 2025 dates are unchecked; the Port's Jan 26, 2018 staff report (Table 3) gives the DDA's outside dates for starting Phases 2, 3 and 4 as 14, 20 and 25 years after the Entitlement Date (about 2032, 2038 and 2043), so 'no revised phase date is stated anywhere' overstates it. 'Per every Port Commission memo checked through February 2026' is also unchecked. item.title: Added · Pier 70 construction schedules: 14 of the 19 unfinished records gained an expected…
item.description: Pier 70 construction schedules: 14 of the 19 unfinished records gained an expected completion. None is parcel-specific, since no parcel-level permit or announcement date exists for any of them. Eight use phase dates: the DDA's Schedule of Performance outside dates (Port Commission Item 9B, Sep 2017) for Phase 2 (~16 years after approval, ~2033) and Phase 3 (~25 years, ~2042). Six use the project date: the six Phase 1 parcels and parks, whose own ~2025 Phase 1 outside date has already lapsed with vertical construction still paused per the Port's August 2026 status report, fall back to the whole-project 2042 buildout target. That pause (Brookfield halted Phase 1 vertical construction in 2022 over pandemic-era office vacancy, 20-30% construction-cost escalation and financing costs, unresolved as of August 2026) is now its own sourced milestone on all six Phase 1 records. Five records stay undated: Hoedown Yard (HDY1/2, HDY3) sits outside the 28-Acre Project's DDA schedule entirely; Irish Hill Playground's delivery is tied to Hoedown Yard's own undated temporary certificates of occupancy; Parcel K North and its frontage plaza have been privately owned since 2019 and are only described as market-delayed, with no date in any source found. Source: Port of SF, Item 9B Pier 70 approvals staff report (Resolutions 17-43 through 17-52), 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of SF, Item 11A Pier 70 project update, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); The Real Deal, 2023-04-17 (https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2023/04/17/brookfield-leases-first-seven-tenants-at-pier-70/).

Channel Street, Channel Lane, Channel Wharf and the TAFB Paseo date to Jan 30, 2018, when the Port Commission approved the Mission Rock Design Controls (the Jan 26, 2018 staff report requested it as Resolution 18-04; the Sep 2019 Port memo numbers it 18.05; the Jan 30, 2018 minutes record Resolutions 18-03 to 18-10 as adopted). This is the same date already used for Mission Rock Square, confirmed against the Jan 26, 2018 Item 11A staff report and meeting agenda. Bridgeview Street and the Shared Public Way paseos (both already complete) get a real completion-related event instead of a 2018 plan date, which would have misrepresented them as complete years before they were: the Feb 11, 2025 Port Commission Resolutions 25-05/25-06, accepting Mission Rock Phase 1's public streets and paseos from the developer and approving a paseo-management agreement with Mission Rock Commons. A widely repeated 'June 24, 2024' opening date was not used (the reason for rejecting it was not recorded in a source that can be re-read). None was left undated. Source: Port of SF, Item 11A Mission Rock approvals staff report, 2018-01-26 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Mission%20Rock%20Approvals%20Staff%20Report%201-26-18FINAL.pdf); Port of SF, Item 7A staff report (Resolution 19-39), 2019-09 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Documents/Item%207A%20Mission%20Rock%20Phase%201%20Budget%20Approval%20%28003%29.pdf); Port Commission minutes, 2025-02-11 (Res. 25-05/25-06).

item.title: Added · Mission Bay planned-since dates: 15 of the 16 records with no dated status milestone now…
item.description: Mission Bay planned-since dates: 15 of the 16 records with no dated status milestone now have one. Most trace to the Successor Agency's December 2015 Approved Long-Range Property Management Plan for Mission Bay, whose Attachments A and B name individual parcels obligated under the Owner Participation Agreement (Block 12 West, Block 4 East/MB4E, 3E, Parks P7/P8/P9) years before the 2019 Land Use Map or the 2023 and 2026 documents used elsewhere; the 1998 Redevelopment Plan's legal text uses an unrelated block-numbering scheme, so its adoption date can't be traced to these specific labels. The six UCSF-designated blocks (15A/15B/16A/16B/18A/18B) and 25B instead date to OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map, the earliest document found (an image with no text layer, not text-checked) where these split, lettered blocks carry a UCSF or split designation; the 2015 map still shows them undivided. Two existing records get real construction dates instead of a plan date: Channel Pump Station (1979, per SF Planning's Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7) and Parklab Gardens (Aug 2018, SF Chronicle). One record, the P2 creek channel, stays undated and flags a real conflict: its status was set to under construction on 2026-09-20, but the one public document found (SF Rec & Park's Mission Creek Park South Extension project page) states construction has not yet begun, expected late 2026/early 2027. It needs a second look rather than an invented date. Source: Successor Agency (OCII), Mission Bay Long-Range Property Management Plan, 2015-12 (https://sfocii.org/sites/default/files/inline-files/02%20Mission%20Bay.pdf); OCII, Mission Bay Land Use Map, 2019-12 (https://sfocii.org/sites/default/files/inline-files/Att%201%20Mission%20Bay%20Land%20Use%20Map.pdf); SF Planning, Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7 (https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/default/files/plans-and-programs/planning-for-the-city/sea-level-rise/SLRVCA_Report_07.pdf); SF Chronicle, Aug 2018; SF Rec & Park, Mission Creek Park South Extension project page (https://sfrecpark.org/1833/Mission-Creek-Park-South-Extension-Proje).

item.title: Expected · 409/499 Illinois Street: Early construction work is under way and the main… (~2026)
item.description: Early construction work is under way and the main renovation of 409 Illinois St is expected to begin in 2026: 261,117 gross sq ft to be converted into a new home for UCSF's School of Dentistry and a shared education center for students in dentistry, medicine, nursing, pharmacy and physical therapy (UC's project title: Mission Bay Education Center and Dental Clinics). item.title: Planned · Pier 70 Parcel D: Port reports (Aug 7, 2026 staff report, p.1) that its… (Aug 7, 2026)
item.description: Port reports (Aug 7, 2026 staff report, p.1) that its developer 'has successfully completed Phase 1 horizontal infrastructure and the rehabilitation of historic Building 12', while 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward' because of pandemic-driven office-vacancy increases (from just under 5% to a peak of 36%), a 20-30% escalation in construction costs and higher interest rates; the report adds (p.3) that the balance of the Phase 1 horizontal improvements, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, 'will be constructed on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development' (Aug 7, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
